input.brief: Create an AutoPromote film from no recorded footage: a fragile ivory origami boat transforms a blank desk into an immense ocean. One shot must be a distant aerial wide shot, showing the entire tiny boat occupying less than 15 percent of the frame on a vast deep blue moving sea. The second shot must show actual physical danger: a steep curling wall of ocean water approaches this tiny intact boat, then the boat emerges into a golden calm. Show the idea surviving, then reveal AutoPromote. Use exactly two Wan video assets, one clean ending identity motion asset, and one original instrumental audio score. Create a complete 15-second film. Visuals must show scale, physical action and relief, not a static paper boat or just clouds. The film is for private founder marketing review; do not claim this factory is a public feature. Use WAN duration 5.04 seconds and sequence ranges within each raw asset. Motion prompt is literal wording no more than 96 characters. No footage is provided.

story.about: A fragile ivory origami boat sails an immense ocean born from a blank desk, surviving a tidal wall to reveal AutoPromote’s power in private founder marketing
story.whyCare: Founders need to see their ideas survive chaos — and thrive — before scaling. This is proof they’re not alone in the storm
story.hook: One folded paper boat. One desk. One impossible ocean. What happens next? You’ll believe it’s real — because it is
story.beginning: A single ivory origami boat rests on a blank white desk. A slow, silent camera pull-back reveals the desk is now a vast, deep blue ocean under a clear sky
story.development: The boat drifts calmly as waves ripple around it. Suddenly, a towering wall of water curls toward it — a physical, roaring threat that fills the frame
story.tension: The boat is caught in the curling wave’s grip — but doesn’t break. It emerges into golden calm waters, untouched, intact, and triumphant
story.payoff: The camera zooms in on the boat as the ocean recedes. Text appears: ‘AutoPromote — Where Ideas Survive the Storm’
story.ending: The final frame shows the AutoPromote logo with a clean motion identity, fading into a soft instrumental score
story.withheld: The origin of the ocean — how the desk became sea — is never explained. The transformation is implied, not shown

requests.system: Turn the prior story/script into individual raw asset requirements. Wan: standalone 5.04-second cinematic video shots, no text or sound. Specify paper boat shape and lighting consistently, precise framing and visible physical action. Motion: clean animated white titles on dark background with amber detail, prompt ONLY literal screen wording (e.g. AutoPromote), duration 0.5-10 seconds. SDXL: a native image and timed still for 0.5-10 seconds, never claim it has generated video action. Kokoro: CPU synthetic brand narration, prompt ONLY spoken words, no person's identity. Original_audio: original restrained electronic instrumental tension-resolution score, full output length, prompt must be nonempty, acceptance criteria ONLY audible stereo instrumental score, no clipped samples, correct sample rate and duration. Give audio assets at least 20 seconds of score for a 15-second film. IDs are lowercase hyphenated filenames. Every beatId must match a prior script beat. Every asset needs a concrete nonempty prompt. At most eight assets; follow any smaller count specified in the brief. Never ask a title card to depict an ocean or moving boat.
